newsitem.title: INDIA: Mixed fortunes for Indian cotton.
newsitem.headline: Mixed fortunes for Indian cotton.

text.p: Indian Punjab varieties extended gains while Gujarat varieties suffered a setback on the cotton market on Monday, dealer said.

Punjab cotton rose on the back of a shortage of ready stock amidst dwindling arrivals in the Punjab region. Daily average arrivals from the Punjab region have fallen to 1,000/1,500 rupees bales (170 kg each) due to end-of-season as well as cloudy weather and unseasonal rain.
In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned rose by 25 rupees at 1,625/1,700 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while F-414 climbed up to 1,925/1,975 rupees per maund from 1,910/1,930 rupees.
Gujarat cotton on the other hand suffered a setback as sluggish mill buying prompted profit-taking by stockists at higher levels.
In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan moved down to 13,500/13,700 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) from 13,700/14,200 rupees.
